decisions.statement: A seeded repository holds a commit and a check and the warrants and an agent's record.
One set of bodies is seeded once and copied for each repository asked for.
Every repository seeded here goes when the test file that asked for one ends.
A body seeded is recorded as read.
A change writing over a seeded body is warranted.
A write goes up the road a command takes from the arguments to the commit.
The command a run's cost is recorded beside is filed in the index a seeded repository carries.
Nothing here reaches the repository this repository is seeded from.
A seeded repository leaves its own index untracked, as a checkout does.
What excludes the index is reached from here rather than spelled beside each fixture.

definition: a scratch akasha repository a change can be landed into
